facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old nulliparous woman presented 14 months after a supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
menorrhagia, pelvic pain, and large uterine leiomyomas
normal Pap smear
no chest radiograph or endometrial biopsy was obtained
an 18–20-week–size uterus (1518 g) was removed via prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag
superficial pelvic endometriosis was noted and cauterized
weakly proliferative endometrium without atypia, adenomyosis, and leiomyoma
left lower quadrant pain, persistent cough, and shortness of breath
firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex
multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest
poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis
grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma

concepts.why: The patient has a firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex, with a biopsy showing grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
The patient has multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, with a biopsy showing grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
The patient has a biopsy showing poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis.
The patient has superficial pelvic endometriosis noted and cauterized during surgery.
The patient has a history of large uterine leiomyomas.
The patient has adenomyosis noted in the pathology report.

rationales.F02: The presence of menorrhagia, pelvic pain, and large uterine leiomyomas suggests a possible diagnosis of leiomyoma.
rationales.F06: The presence of superficial pelvic endometriosis suggests a possible diagnosis of endometriosis.
rationales.F07: The presence of weakly proliferative endometrium without atypia, adenomyosis, and leiomyoma suggests a possible diagnosis of leiomyoma and adenomyosis.
rationales.F11: The presence of poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis suggests a possible diagnosis of poorly differentiated carcinoma.
rationales.F12: The presence of grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma suggests a possible diagnosis of endometrioid adenocarcinoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, and grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma, suggest a disseminated cancer, which is more specific than a localized endometrioid adenocarcinoma
